inputs.original_text: An Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law earlier this month after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued that it burdened religious freedom by limiting abortions. That turns a foundational liberty on its head: religious freedom should protect conscience, not become a blanket excuse to override laws meant to protect unborn life. When courts accept that reasoning, they put abortion ideology ahead of the moral and social duty to defend the most vulnerable.
inputs.modified_text: An Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law earlier this month after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice claimed it burdened religious freedom by limiting abortion. That argument turns liberty on its head: conscience deserves protection, but it should not become a tool for defeating laws meant to defend unborn life. When courts put abortion claims ahead of the duty to protect the most vulnerable, they weaken the moral foundations a society depends on.
